one_liner: Meta’s Threads Graph API lets apps post on behalf of a user, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, run keyword/profile discovery, and fetch insights.
access_notes: Create a Meta app and select the “Threads” use case; permissions for non‑role users require App Review; webhooks require Live/advanced access and business verification.
mcp_notes: No official MCP from Meta; multiple third‑party/open‑source MCP servers exist that wrap the Threads API.
blocker_notes: Production‑grade usage requires App Review, Live mode/advanced access, and business verification.

evidence.quote: API authentication is handled by Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol… Short‑lived access tokens are valid for 1 hour…
Long‑lived tokens are valid for 60 days and can be refreshed…
For app users without a role on your app… each permission must first be approved through the App Review process, and your app must be published.
Publishing posts requires… ‘threads_basic’… ‘threads_content_publish’… If your app has not been approved for advanced access… you can only post on behalf of Threads testers…
For non‑tech providers, the apps must be in Live mode… For tech providers, the apps must have permissions with an advanced access level… The business connected to the app must be verified.
